title: Rethinking Joint Maximum Mean Discrepancy for Visual Domain Adaptation

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2, sentence 'has achieved 1.4%/0.8% and 0.9%/0.8% improvements on the two datasets, respectively'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For Office-31, the text claims a 0.8% improvement for OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC over OGL2P, but Table 1 shows OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC = 90.1 and OGL2P = 90.7, which is a decrease of 0.6%, not an improvement.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2, sentence 'OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC achieves the best average results among all compared approaches, with 0.3% and 0.5% improvements over the second-best method, i.e., RSDA-MSTN'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: On Office-31, RSDA-MSTN achieves 91.2 (Table 1) while the reported OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC average is 90.1, a drop of 1.1 points, not a 0.3% improvement. The claim of best performance is therefore false.

Table 1 reports OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC average accuracy on Office-31 as 90.1, while Table 3 reports OGLP+JMMD-HSIC as 91.5±1.3 for the same dataset and method. The two numbers are contradictory and cannot both be correct.
The six task accuracies are 96.1, 95.3, 77.6, 98.1, 77.1, 99.1, whose true mean is (96.1+95.3+77.6+98.1+77.1+99.1)/6 = 90.55, but the table states 90.1. This is a miscalculation (off by ~0.9).

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The introduction states 'the exact elimination of the tensor product remains an open problem,' whereas the abstract and Section 3.1 present a derived concise JMMD that avoids the tensor-product operator.
